## KernelSeal v1.1.0

Signed releases, a published SBOM, and the node probe that v1.0.0's notes told you
to run but did not ship. No change to the agent, the shim, or the BPF programs:
the protection guarantee is identical to v1.0.0.

### Releases are now signed

Images and artifacts are signed with [cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign)
keyless signing. There is no public key to distribute. The signature carries a
short-lived Sigstore certificate proving which workflow, in which repository, at
which tag produced the artifact, and that identity is what you verify:

```bash
IMAGE=ghcr.io/phonginreallife/kernelseal
VERSION=v1.1.0
IDENTITY="https://github.com/phonginreallife/kernelseal/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/${VERSION}"

cosign verify \
  --certificate-identity "$IDENTITY" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  "${IMAGE}:${VERSION}"
```

Both flags are required. `cosign verify` without them accepts a signature from any
identity, which is the most common way this check gets run and proves nothing.

Signatures attach to the image digest rather than the tag, because a tag can later
be moved to a different image while a digest cannot. Resolve the digest and deploy
that:

```bash
crane digest "${IMAGE}:${VERSION}"
```

The release tarballs are covered by a signature over `checksums.txt`, since that
file contains their hashes:

```bash
cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle checksums.txt.cosign.bundle \
  --certificate-identity "$IDENTITY" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  checksums.txt

sha256sum -c checksums.txt
```

`SECURITY.md` previously documented signature verification against signatures that
were never produced. That is fixed in both directions: the signatures exist, and
the instructions match what actually signs them.

### SBOM

An SPDX SBOM ships as a release asset and as a cosign attestation on the image, so
a cluster that only knows a digest can still recover the bill of materials:

```bash
cosign verify-attestation --type spdxjson \
  --certificate-identity "$IDENTITY" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  "${IMAGE}:${VERSION}" | jq -r .payload | base64 -d | jq .predicate > sbom.json
```

### The node probe

`deploy/kernelseal-probe.yaml` is in the repository. It was referenced by the
v1.0.0 release notes without ever having been committed, so following those notes
failed on a missing file. Apologies if you hit that.

```bash
kubectl apply -f deploy/kernelseal-probe.yaml
kubectl logs -f job/kernelseal-probe
kubectl delete -f deploy/kernelseal-probe.yaml
```

It answers the only question that matters before deploying anything: whether the
node's kernel lists `bpf` as an active LSM. It runs in `audit` mode with no secret
bindings, so nothing can be blocked and no secret is read, and it loads and
attaches for real, because every static check can pass on a node where the attach
still fails.

### Breaking change for importers

The Go module path is now `github.com/phonginreallife/kernelseal`. It was
`kernelseal`, which the toolchain cannot resolve, so the packages could not be
imported and the binaries could not be installed with `go install`.

This breaks any existing import of these packages. Update the prefix:

```
kernelseal/internal/...  ->  github.com/phonginreallife/kernelseal/internal/...
```

Nothing about the built binaries or the deployment changes.

### Documentation

- The Kubernetes path now reads probe, then sidecar, then DaemonSet. The DaemonSet
  is no longer presented first, because a node-wide agent serves one socket to
  every pod that mounts it and socket reachability is the authorization boundary.
  The per-pod sidecar is the pattern to start with.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` and a code of conduct, issue forms, and a pull request
  template.
- A [roadmap issue](https://github.com/phonginreallife/kernelseal/issues/16)
  collecting the known gaps: unimplemented `vaultRef`, the parsed but unused
  selectors, the agent restart gap, fork inheritance, and heap residue.

### CI

Two secret scanners were not working, and had not been since before v1.0.0, because
GitHub had disabled the Security workflow for inactivity:

- **TruffleHog was scanning nothing.** Its `base` was the default branch, which on
  a push to `main` is the same commit as `head`, so it diffed a commit against
  itself, reported zero bytes scanned, and passed. Pushes now scan the push range
  and the weekly run scans the full history. That full scan has now read this
  repository's entire history for the first time and found nothing.
- **Gitleaks was failing** on a false positive in `scripts/run-node-demo.sh`,
  where the `curl-auth-header` rule matched a shell variable holding a
  locally-minted demo JWT.

### Upgrade

Nothing to do beyond replacing the binaries or the image. No config changes, no
BPF object changes, no behavior changes.

```bash
ghcr.io/phonginreallife/kernelseal:v1.1.0
```
